svg.title: Chiral DMI Boundary Canting and Interface-Normal Realization
svg.desc: Two-panel diagram of Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya boundary conditions in Fullmag: (a) numerically solved Rohart and Thiaville edge canting profile m_z(x) and boundary spin tilt under 2A d_nu m + D[(n_hat x nu) x m] = 0, and (b) comparison of FDM fixed +z_hat interface normal with ghost boundary correction versus FEM general normalized interface normal n_hat carrying the natural boundary integral weakly.
svg.text: Chiral DMI Boundary Canting and Interface-Normal Realization
Natural boundary law 2A ∂ν m + D[(n̂ × ν) × m] = 0 (Rohart & Thiaville 2013), solved canting profile, and FDM vs FEM normals
Solved 1D Euler–Lagrange BVP: A = 15 pJ/m, Keff = 0.30 MJ/m³, L = 80 nm (ℓDMI = 2A/|D|)
Interfacial DMI + Exchange Natural BC: 2A ∂ν m + D [(n̂ × ν) × m] = 0 on ∂Ωm
Boundary slope dθ/dx|±L/2 = −D/(2A); drops mz at edges and creates chiral edge confinement potential.
FDM Fixed +ẑ vs FEM General Normal n̂
Discrete realization of interface symmetry and natural boundary terms
FDM CPU / CUDA: Canonical +ẑ Interface Normal Only
ΔHx = −(D / μ0 Ms Δx) mz, ΔHz = +(D / μ0 Ms Δx) mx
Fail-closed planner gate: any tilted n̂ ≠ +ẑ on FDM is rejected (no rotated stencil).
Decoupled touching objects or zero inter-region A also fail closed if DMI is active.
FEM CPU / CUDA: General Normalized Normal n̂ & Weak Form
Weak residual integrates volume first variation:
Integration by parts carries natural boundary term:
δEi∂Ω = D ∫∂Ω_m [(n̂ × ν) × m] · v dS
No separate boundary integral needed (avoids double-counting).
Contrast: Isotropic Bulk DMI Natural Boundary Law
2A ∂ν m + Db (m × ν) = 0 on ∂Ωm (characteristic twist scale ℓDMI = 2A / |Db|)
• No interface normal n̂ exists; tangential surface twist is proportional to m × ν.
• FEM carries this naturally in weak residual; non-periodic FDM Bulk DMI is planner-rejected.
